column1: # GE-T10's surname set: a subject the question names by the last word of a name the store
# WHY. "Warum wirkte Listers Karbolsäure?" finds no subject: rule 29 takes the genitive off,
# and `Lister` is still not a name the store writes, which is "Joseph Lister". Three of the
# corpus's people are written that way (John Snow, James Lind, Joseph Lister, and the Russian
# spellings of each), and a question names a person by the surname more often than not.
# THE RULE, DECLARED before a word of this set was written; scored first without it
# (`baseline.txt`), and not changed after a run:
#  33. a surname for a name: when no pass finds any run, a single word written with a capital
#      that is the last word of an entity's name of more than one word names that entity — as
#      spelled, ignoring case; in German, also without its genitive `s` or `'` (rule 29's
#      ending); and through the question's language's stemmer, which cuts both alike
#      (`Листера`, `Листер`). Last, behind the spelled, stemmed and derived passes, so that no
#      question any of them reads changes; and the last word only, since a given name is shared
#      far more often than a surname. Two entities with the surname are SMY-W417, as any two are.
# THE SET. Columns: qid, subject, lang, question. `subject` is the entity label the question is
# about, or `none` for one that names nobody the store writes and should find no subject. The
# `-g` rows are guards: a given name alone, and a lower-case word that spells a surname. The
# `-p` rows are the rule's price, declared with it: a question that names its subject by the
# surname and another subject in full finds the other, since the earlier passes read it first.
# WHO WROTE THIS. The hand that declared the rule, after declaring it. Single hand.
